subject: math

objective.text: Use square tiles to compose a rectangle, and relate to the array model.

explanations.title: Rectangle with no gaps
explanations.text: Put the tiles in rows with no spaces between them. The tiles make a rectangle. It has corners like an L.

explanations.title: Rows or columns, same rectangle
explanations.text: 2 rows of 5 and 2 columns of 5 use the same 10 tiles. It is the same rectangle turned on its side. Both are 2 groups of 5.

explanations.title: A square is a special rectangle
explanations.text: A square has the same number of rows and columns. 3 rows of 3 is a square. 4 rows of 4 is a square.

explanations.title: Not every number makes a square
explanations.text: Some numbers cannot make equal rows and columns. 10 tiles can only make 2 rows of 5 or 1 row of 10.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2 (S: Only certain numbers)

examples.title: 2 rows of 5
examples.text: 10 tiles in 2 rows of 5. 5 plus 5 equals 10. The shape is a rectangle.

examples.title: 15 tiles and 12 tiles
examples.text: 3 by 5 uses 15 tiles. 3 by 4 uses 12 tiles. Both are rectangles.

examples.title: 3 rows of 3
examples.text: Take one row from 3 columns of 4. Now there are 3 rows and 3 columns. It is a square.

examples.title: 16 tiles in a square
examples.text: 4 rows of 4 tiles. 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 4 equals 16. It is a square.
